what_it_does: This paper pushes the density and efficiency of SRAM (Static RAM—the fast cache memory inside processors) to new limits in Intel's latest 18A generation chips (sub-2 nanometer). The challenge: as transistors shrink, traditional 6-transistor SRAM bitcells hit scaling limits—they need higher voltages to function reliably, which wastes power. The solution combines two innovations. First, the transistor design itself becomes more flexible using RibbonFET technology (a new transistor shape that allows width tuning), letting the designers optimize each transistor individually for the best read and write performance without extra power-hungry assist circuitry. Second, they use PowerVia, a backside power delivery technology that runs power rails beneath the chip on the bottom metal layers rather than on top, freeing up valuable routing space and reducing power supply noise (droop). Together these achieve unprecedented density (0.021 square micrometers per bit) while keeping the minimum operating voltage low, saving power.
